name: Genesis
author: Traditionally Moses.
date: Traditionally linked to the time of Moses, about 1400 to 1200 BC. The events span from creation to about 1800 BC.
setting: Written for Israel before entering the promised land. It tells where the world, sin, and the chosen family came from.
theme: God creates a good world, sin breaks it, and God begins a plan to bless all nations through Abraham’s family.

outline.label: Creation in six days and the Sabbath
Eden, the fall, and the first family
Joseph and the family in Egypt

christInBook: Genesis plants the promise of an offspring who will crush the serpent (3:15) and bless all nations through Abraham’s line (12:3). Judah’s line carries the scepter (49:10), and Isaac, Joseph, and the ram caught in the thicket all look ahead to the sacrifice and rescue God would provide.
howToRead: Read Genesis as the foundation for everything after it. Watch for repeated patterns: a promise, a threat to the promise, and God’s faithful rescue. The genealogies are not filler. They trace the line of promise from Adam through Abraham to the twelve tribes.
